name: stateful-processing
context: Aggregations, joins and windowed computations must remember what came before — a running count per key, the last N minutes of a join's other side, an accumulating session. This pattern keeps that memory local to the processing task, co-located with the partitions it serves, and makes it recoverable by writing every state change to a durable changelog before or atomically with committing the input offset. The changelog is the source of truth; the local store is a cache rebuilt from it.
benefits: Enables joins and aggregations at scale without a remote query per record — lookups are local to the task
Fault tolerance comes from replay, not from checkpointing the whole working set: a failed task rebuilds its store from the changelog
Partitioning gives both parallelism and locality: the state for a key is only ever touched by the task owning that key's partition
Exactly-once becomes achievable end to end when input offsets, changelog writes and output records commit atomically
Named, stable state stores and changelog topics make rolling redeployment of an evolving topology safe
tradeoffs: State growth is unbounded unless retention is explicit — windowed aggregation keys are (key, window), so log compaction can never purge old entries
Local stores are caches with uncontrolled flush timing; a crash can leave the store holding writes never committed to the changelog
Under exactly-once semantics without transactional state stores, a crash wipes the entire local store and replays the changelog — observed delays have spanned days for high-cardinality tables
Every key-changing operation before a stateful operator injects a repartition topic, adding a hop and reordering the stream
State is queryable only from inside the application; serving it externally means adding interactive-query APIs or a second store
use_cases: Per-key counters and running aggregates maintained incrementally as records arrive
Stream-table enrichment where a compacted changelog supplies the latest reference value locally
Windowed aggregation with results emitted continuously and corrected as late data arrives
Exactly-once pipelines writing to Kafka and to external transactional sinks
Interactive queries served directly from the application's own state stores
avoid_when: The computation is a pure function of a single record — stateless processing has none of these costs
The key space is unbounded and no retention, windowing or compaction policy can be agreed
The team cannot operate long-running stateful processes with restart-and-replay semantics
Strong cross-key consistency is required — local per-key state cannot provide it
component_types: State store: local key-value or windowed store embedded in each task, backed by a cache (in-memory map or RocksDB)
Changelog topic: compacted durable log of state changes; the authoritative copy of the state
Cache layer: non-fault-tolerant local store used for lookups, rebuilt from the changelog
Commit protocol: periodic flush of stores plus offset commit, or a transaction spanning offsets, changelog and output
Transactional buffer: holds state writes until the corresponding changelog transaction commits
Repartition topic: internal topic inserted when a key-changing operator precedes a stateful one
anti_patterns: Relying on the local store for durability — the changelog is the source of truth and the local store is only a cache
Leaving state stores unnamed, so generated names shift when an operator is inserted earlier and a rolling redeployment becomes a topology-breaking change
Assuming exactly-once makes local state consistent: without transactional state stores a crash still wipes and replays the store
Applying a key-changing operator before every aggregation, silently doubling the network cost of the pipeline
Letting windowed state accumulate without retention, because log compaction can never purge (key, window) entries
design_principles: The log is the source of truth; local state is a rebuildable cache
State locality: keep all state for a key on the single task that owns that key's partition
Atomicity across offsets, changelog and output, or the guarantee is not actually exactly-once
Explicit retention for every store — bounded by design, not by luck
Stable, user-supplied names for state stores and repartition topics so topology evolution is not a breaking change
best_practices: Always name state stores and repartition topics explicitly; unnamed internal topics shift when the topology changes
Size commit intervals against recovery cost — a longer interval replays more, a shorter one costs more throughput
Use segment-based local stores for windowed state so memory is bounded by retention rather than by key cardinality
Monitor changelog lag and local store size separately; they fail for different reasons
Assume the local store will be discarded — test recovery by killing tasks, not by reading the happy path
references: Apache Kafka, Core Concepts — States, Aggregations, Windowing and processing guarantees, https://kafka.apache.org/43/streams/core-concepts/
Apache Kafka, Streams Architecture — state stores, fault tolerance and recovery, https://kafka.apache.org/43/streams/architecture/

Matthias Sax, Kafka Streams Internal Data Management (changelog topic is the source of truth; RocksDB is a non-fault-tolerant cache), https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=65864917
KIP-844: Transactional State Stores — why crash failure wipes and replays state today, https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/display/KAFKA/KIP-844%3A+Transactional+State+Stores
